title: Correct and complete the firstmate explainer page to reach 4 of 5
summary: The firstmate explainer (built by `xtask site` from `studies/firstmate-work-handling`) rated 3 by its audience and 2 by readers who checked it against firstmate's source. I read this as: fix what the page gets wrong and fill in what it leaves out, mainly in `intro.json` and the study claims and model. Newcomers are the audience, and the page must stay cited and buildable.

defaults_applied.how: Every new or corrected statement on the page cites claims with source quotes from the pinned firstmate commit; unmeasured items are labeled.
Wording is rewritten for a newcomer who has never seen firstmate.
cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass, with a site test added if the structure changes.
The verifier builds the page with xtask site and checks the claim-to-source citations.
The accuracy and completeness of the study content is fixed, not just the few phrases reviewers named.
The missing specifics were recovered from the repository's study files and the design note.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience is newcomers to firstmate who read only the page; the reviewers who check against firstmate's source are the stricter judges, so factual accuracy is the main lever on the rating.

The request does not list the specific errors. I could not see firstmate's source or the reviewers' notes, so the producer must re-read the pinned commit (pin.json) to find them. My gap list comes from reading the page's own claims and model and is not exhaustive.
The study stays a single pinned commit and all content stays in the existing JSON files; no new rendering features, script, or diagram are added.
Corrections that change claims or model must keep the study validators in crates/athena-cap-study passing; validation.json is regenerated only if the validator requires it.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every firstmate fact in intro.json, claims.json and model.json that changed is backed by a claim whose quote appears in the pinned firstmate source at the pinned commit; the summary of the change lists each factual correction and each addition, with the source path and lines.

The page's Start here section and transition cards state what a newcomer needs and the current page omits or blurs. This includes the failure and limit behaviour already in the claims: lock contention exits 1 without waiting, an unreadable capacity exits 1, relaunch failure restores the record, no retry or relaunch bound was found, and a missing session start leaves a close unreplayed. It also corrects the over-simplified merge-authority wording, since yolo is a configured setting and the claim says the 'configured merge authority', and the glossary entry for 'ship'.
Placeholder values the study model carries (guard 'none' with evaluator 'agent' on t5, t7, t8) are not presented to a reader as if the agent evaluates a guard; the page says no guard applies.

Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site --out <dir>` from the repository root with a fresh out path inside the working directory. It exits 0 and writes index.html. Every cited claim id resolves and no intro element, glossary term or transition summary is uncited.
`cargo test --workspace` passes, including the xtask site tests and the study-capability validation tests, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
If the intro or lead-in structure changes, docs/design/explainer-site.md describes it; no governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) changes.

out_of_scope: Studying additional firstmate mechanisms beyond work handling, or a different pinned commit
An expert track, replay view, drawn state diagram or custom domain
departures: Higher cost and lower pass odds than the reference: the request names no specific defects, the firstmate source is not in this copy, and the verifier must judge factual accuracy against a source it may not be able to read.
